Chapter 8. The Universe as a Web of Meaning.
Have you ever stepped outside on a clear night, looked up at the stars, and just felt... overwhelmed? There’s something about that vastness—a kind of silence that somehow makes you feel like you belong. For a moment, everything else fades away, and it’s as if the universe is whispering that you’re part of something bigger. That feeling—that sense of connection—it’s real.
The holographic model suggests it’s not just wishful thinking. If every tiny part of the universe carries information about the whole, then meaning isn’t something we simply make up. It’s woven right into the fabric of existence.
You can see this idea in the stories people share, especially during times of loss or change. Imagine someone grieving a loved one, and then, out of nowhere, a favorite song comes on the radio—or a sudden breeze stirs the air, or a dream feels more real than waking life. Sure, these things could be coincidence. But sometimes, they just feel too meaningful to ignore, don’t they?
For a lot of us, searching for meaning is a lifelong journey. Some people look for it in faith, others in creativity, science, or helping others. But underneath it all, there’s that same longing—to feel connected, to believe that life really does matter. The holographic model invites us to see this longing as something more than a personal need—it’s a reflection of how the universe itself is intertwined.
Meaning, then, isn’t something we keep to ourselves—it’s something we share. The stories we tell, the rituals we keep, the symbols we hold dear—they’re all ways of tuning in to the deeper patterns at work in our lives. Even difficult times—our struggles and pain—can teach us to see the world in new ways, if we let them.
Think of a teacher standing in front of a classroom, wondering if anything she says is actually making a difference. Then, years later, a former student comes back—remembering just one conversation that changed everything for him. Suddenly, that teacher realizes: meaning isn’t always obvious, but it’s always there, woven through the relationships that connect us all.
The holographic model invites us to stop seeing ourselves as isolated individuals. Instead, we’re all part of a vast, unfolding story—a story where every thought, every action, every moment carries weight. And that’s a pretty amazing way to look at the universe, isn’t it?
